meta.title: Threats, harassment, or blackmail: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

harassment.title: Threats, harassment, or blackmail
harassment.subtitle: Someone is threatening you, harassing you, or trying to blackmail you online, and you want to report it.
harassment.whatThisIsBody: This covers being threatened, stalked, or harassed through messages, calls, or social media, and blackmail or sextortion, where someone demands money or more content by threatening to share private images or information.
harassment.notBuiltBody: There is no reporting flow for this on this prototype. Only one journey is finished end to end: money taken from a bank account or UPI. This page is a real, honest stop, not a form in disguise.
harassment.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: India's national cybercrime helpline. It covers harassment, threats, and blackmail, not just financial fraud.

steps.title: Report on the real national portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a dedicated "Women/Children Related Crime" section, including an option to report anonymously without giving your name.

steps.title: Don't delete anything
steps.body: Keep the messages, screenshots, and profile or number involved exactly as they are. They may be needed as evidence.

steps.title: Don't pay, and don't engage further
steps.body: Paying blackmail rarely ends the demands. Screenshot everything and stop replying, then report it.

harassment.moneyNote: If money was also taken from you as part of this, our one finished journey covers that part.

meta.title: Hacked account, or something else happened: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

hacked.title: Hacked account, or something else happened
hacked.subtitle: Your account, email, or online profile was taken over, or what happened to you doesn't fit anywhere else on this page.
hacked.whatThisIsBody: This covers a hacked email, social media, or other online account, someone impersonating you online, ransomware, and anything else that doesn't fit "money was taken from my account".
hacked.notBuiltBody: There is no reporting flow for this on this prototype. Only one journey is finished end to end: money taken from a bank account or UPI. This page is a real, honest stop, not a form in disguise.
hacked.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Secure the account first
steps.body: If you can still log in, change the password immediately and turn on two-factor authentication. If you can't log in, use the platform's own account-recovery flow.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: India's national cybercrime helpline. It handles hacked accounts and impersonation, not just financial fraud.

steps.title: Report on the real national portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has an "Other Cyber Crime" category that covers hacking, unauthorized access, and cases that don't fit elsewhere.

steps.title: Don't delete anything
steps.body: Keep screenshots, login-alert emails, and any message from the attacker exactly as they are. They may be needed as evidence.

hacked.moneyNote: If money was also taken from you as part of this, our one finished journey covers that part.

meta.title: Check a suspect: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

check-suspect.title: Check a suspect (number, email, website, or app)
check-suspect.subtitle: You want to check whether a phone number, email address, website, or app has already been reported as a suspect before you trust it.
check-suspect.whatThisIsBody: On the real national portal, this is the Suspect Repository: a lookup where you can check a mobile number, email address, website, or app name against entries built from prior citizen complaints, before you trust it with money or personal information.
check-suspect.notBuiltBody: There is no suspect-lookup database on this prototype. Building one honestly would need access to the real repository of reported suspects, which we don't have and won't fake with made-up entries. Only one journey is finished end to end: money taken from a bank account or UPI.
check-suspect.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Use the real Suspect Repository
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a live Suspect Repository where you can check a mobile number, email, website, or app before you trust it.

steps.title: Verify payment details independently
steps.body: Before paying anyone, confirm their identity through a channel you already trust, your bank's official app or a company's official website, not a link or number they gave you.

steps.title: Call 1930 if you're mid-scam
steps.body: If you're in the middle of a suspicious call or payment request right now, call before you send anything else.

check-suspect.moneyNote: If a suspect you were checking already took money from you, our one finished journey covers that part.

meta.title: Report a suspect: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

report-suspect.title: Report a suspect to I4C, or report abuse to a social platform
report-suspect.subtitle: You want to flag a suspicious number, account, or website to the authorities, or report abusive content to the platform hosting it.
report-suspect.whatThisIsBody: This covers two related but different actions: reporting a suspect (a number, account, website, or app used in cybercrime) to I4C so it can be added to the Suspect Repository, and reporting abusive content directly to the social media platform that hosts it, using that platform's own reporting tools.
report-suspect.notBuiltBody: Neither of these is built on this prototype. Reporting a suspect to I4C needs access to the real repository we don't have; reporting abuse to a platform depends on that platform's own systems, not ours.
report-suspect.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Report abusive content on the platform itself
steps.body: WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, X, and YouTube each have their own in-app report button. That report goes straight to the platform and works today, right now.

steps.title: Report the suspect on the real portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a dedicated flow for reporting a suspect number, account, or website to I4C.

steps.title: File your own complaint if you're a victim
steps.body: If this suspect took money from you, our one finished journey covers writing it up and getting a Complaint ID.

report-suspect.moneyNote: If the suspect you're reporting also took money from you, our one finished journey covers that part.

meta.title: Volunteer registration, login, and terms: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

volunteer-account.title: Cyber volunteer registration, login, and terms
volunteer-account.subtitle: You want to create a Cyber Volunteer account, sign in to one, or read the volunteer terms and conditions.
volunteer-account.whatThisIsBody: The real Cyber Volunteer Programme is a genuine account system: citizens register, get verified, and are approved before they can take part. It has its own login, its own terms and conditions, and its own vetting process.
volunteer-account.notBuiltBody: Registration, login, and a real terms-of-service document all need an account and verification system this prototype doesn't build. Inventing a fake login here would be exactly the fake interactivity this project refuses to ship.
volunteer-account.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Read what the real programme actually is
steps.body: Our Cyber Volunteer Concept page explains the real programme honestly, without pretending this prototype runs it.

steps.title: Register on the real portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has the real volunteer registration, login, and terms and conditions.

steps.title: Call 1930 if something feels off
steps.body: If a message or call claiming to be about volunteer registration asks for money or your Aadhaar/PAN, treat it as a scam and report it.

volunteer-account.moneyNote: If someone impersonating the volunteer programme took money from you, our one finished journey covers that part.

media-gallery.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. steps.title: Read our own safety content instead
steps.body: Our Cyber Safety Tips and Cyber Awareness pages are real, written content, not stock media, and cover the same ground.

steps.title: See the real gallery

media-gallery.moneyNote: If you're here after losing money and want to file a report instead, our one finished journey covers that.

meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

daily-digest.title: Daily digest
daily-digest.subtitle: You want a daily summary of newly published cyber-security advisories and trends.
daily-digest.whatThisIsBody: The real portal publishes a daily digest of newly reported advisories and trends, refreshed every day.
daily-digest.notBuiltBody: Building this honestly would mean either connecting to a real, live incident feed we don't have, or inventing today's numbers ourselves. We refuse to do the second one, so there is no digest here, not a fake one with made-up figures.
daily-digest.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Read our general advisories instead
steps.body: Our Advisories page covers common, ongoing scam patterns that don't depend on today's date, so it can't go stale or be faked.

steps.title: See the real daily digest
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in publishes the actual day-by-day advisory digest.

daily-digest.moneyNote: If a scam mentioned in an advisory already cost you money, our one finished journey covers filing a report.

screen-reader.title: Dedicated screen reader tool
screen-reader.subtitle: You're looking for a built-in screen-reader tool like the one on the real portal.
screen-reader.whatThisIsBody: The real portal offers a dedicated screen-reader tool bundled into the page that reads content aloud on request.
screen-reader.notBuiltBody: We didn't build a separate screen-reader tool. Instead, every page here is built with semantic HTML, labelled controls, and visible focus states, so your own screen reader, NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, or TalkBack, already works properly, without us needing to bundle one.
screen-reader.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Use your device's own screen reader
steps.body: NVDA or JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on Mac and iOS, TalkBack on Android, all work correctly on this prototype.

steps.title: Read our accessibility statement
steps.body: It lists exactly what's implemented and what hasn't been independently verified yet, honestly.

screen-reader.moneyNote: If you're here to report money that was taken from you, our one finished journey is built to work with a screen reader end to end.

public-notices.title: RTI and CPGRAMS public notices
public-notices.subtitle: You're looking for Right to Information disclosures or CPGRAMS grievance-redress notices published by the department.
public-notices.whatThisIsBody: RTI (Right to Information) public notices and CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) notices are official disclosures a government department is legally required to publish.
public-notices.notBuiltBody: We're an independent hackathon prototype, not a government department. We have no real notices to publish, so we won't invent any to fill this space.
public-notices.whyBody: This is a three day hackathon build. Starting five reporting flows and finishing none of them would have been worse than finishing one properly, so we built the financial fraud journey completely, from writing your story to getting a trackable Complaint ID, and named everything else we didn't get to instead of hiding it. See the full list of <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Use the official RTI and CPGRAMS channels
steps.body: These disclosures are handled by the real government department, not by this prototype, which has no legal standing to publish them.

steps.title: See what this prototype actually is
steps.body: Our what's real vs mocked page states plainly that we are an independent, unaffiliated hackathon build.

public-notices.moneyNote: If you're here to report money that was taken from you, our one finished journey covers that part.
